The evidence supports testing stronger discrimination, but sampled HR@10 cannot establish full-catalog improvement: sampled metrics can reverse model orderings even in expectation ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) supports causal convolutional sequence modeling and discusses sampled-softmax scalability; it does not isolate a negative-count effect from popularity shortcuts. [Scalable Cross-Entropy, RecSys 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.18721v1) provides stronger full-catalog evidence: a common SASRec implementation compares full CE, multi-negative BCE, sampled CE and SCE using unsampled HR/NDCG and catalog coverage. However, memory-budget comparisons vary batch size and sampling parameters, so they are not a clean negative-count-only ablation or proof of popularity debiasing.

[PSL, NeurIPS 2024](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/db1d5c63576587fc1d40d33a75190c71-Paper-Conference.pdf) supplies relevant controls: 1,000 uniform training negatives, popularity-shift evaluation with item-uniform held-out interactions, and injected false-negative probabilities from 0.05–0.5. PSL degrades less than softmax under injected noise, supporting concern about excessive weighting of high-scoring negatives. These are collaborative-filtering experiments, not direct NextItNet evidence. [R2NS, WWW 2026](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) ablates warm-start, global recall, random-negative infusion and curriculum difficulty. Removing random infusion sharply hurts results; harder negatives alone are insufficient. Its evaluation section does not clearly specify sampled versus full-catalog candidates, limiting conclusions about that distinction.

For this experiment, isolate uniform-negative count while fixing NextItNet architecture, seed, updates, positive sampling, loss normalization and tuning budget. Keep pinned sampled validation HR@10 as the selection criterion. Where permitted, diagnose the same validation users with full-catalog ranking, target-popularity strata, recommendation popularity/coverage and shuffled-history sensitivity. Gains surviving these checks would support improved personalized discrimination; sampled HR@10 alone leaves popularity shortcuts unresolved.
